one_month_reasoning: No NVDA print inside the window: Q3 FY27 is expected ~Nov 17 (some calendars Nov 25; not confirmed by the company), after 2026-11-04. In the window: TSMC Q3 results (mid-Oct, AI demand read-through); hyperscaler earnings and 2027 capex guides (late Oct; consensus capex growth slowing to ~+22% in 2027, src 27, so guides above that are upside); FOMC Oct 28 (83% hold / 17% hike on the DeFi Rate aggregate, src 14), with the Dec 9 meeting hike ~70-72% priced (src 14,15), so a hawkish statement with the 10Y at ~5.26% (src 26) is the main macro downside; US midterms Nov 3; AMD earnings early Nov. These are two-sided and largely expected. Stock is at a 52-week high, mild momentum offset by rates. Net: centred at ~$237.6 (+0.3%), monthly sigma ~10.9% (38%/3.5) with a 15% weight on a 1.8x-wider component for capex/macro surprises.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E (consistent-window Oct-2027 NTM EPS $16.7 x 16x = $267, w0.5), FCF yield ($16.7 x 23.9B x 75% conversion at 5.5% + $1 net cash = $230, w0.3) and mid-cycle EPS $13 x 20x = $260 (w0.2): ~$255 for Oct 2027. The 16x is the same multiple used in the base scenario.

Q3FY27 2.47 + Q4 2.73 + Q1FY28 3.17 + Q2 3.63 = $12.00 (src 9); stockanalysis fwd P/E 19.34 implies $12.25 (src 4)

Consensus hyperscaler capex growth decelerates from +84% (2026) to +22% (2027) (src 27); FY29 (~CY2028) NVDA EPS growth set below that capex growth path at +15% (round 1 used +20%), giving FY29 EPS ~$18.1

H2 FY28 $8.90 + H1 FY29 ~48% of $18.1 = $8.67 -> $17.57; less ~5% for memory-cost margin squeeze (Q4 GM 71-72% trough, FY28 72-73%, src 6) and estimate risk = $16.7. Round 1 used the shifted Q4 FY28-Q3 FY29 window ($17.5).

One multiple used in fair value and base scenario. Today 19.3-19.7x NTM (src 4,9) vs ~25x in Apr-2026 (src 10); at-scale anchor AVGO/TSM 20.5-20.7x (src 5). 16x = ~22% below that anchor and 3.5 turns below today, reflecting decelerating growth (+70% FY28 to ~+15% FY29) and 10Y at ~5.26% with a Dec hike ~70-72% priced (src 26,14,15). Not leaning on a '17-20x historical floor' (that mixed an NTM assertion with an LTM statistic).

bear.story: AI-capex digestion: hyperscalers (most FCF-negative in 2027, consensus capex growth already slowing to ~+22%) slow 2028 orders, memory costs push GM toward 70%, ASICs take share. Horizon NTM EPS falls to ~$12.5 and the multiple de-rates to ~12x, as cyclical semis do when estimates roll over: ~$150 (-37%), in line with NVDA's 2018 and 2022 drawdowns.

base.story: FY28 delivers (~+70% revenue, EPS ~$15.7), FY29 grows ~15%; consistent-window NTM EPS ~$16.7. The multiple compresses another 3.5 turns to 16x (same multiple as the fair value) as growth decelerates and the 10Y stays ~5%+: ~$267 (+13%). Break-even is ~14.2x on this EPS, so the base case needs EPS delivery, not a re-rating.

bull.story: Supply-constrained demand extends into FY29 (capex nearer Goldman's $1.1-1.4T), price hikes hold GM at 73%+, rates ease; NTM EPS ~$19 at ~18x (still below today's 19.5x and the AVGO/TSM anchor): ~$342 (+44%).

comps_summary.peer_range: Fwd P/E 6.1x (MU) to 128.9x (ARM); est. fwd EV/EBITDA 4.4x to 125x. The large-cap, high-earnings cluster (AVGO 20.5x, TSM 20.7x, QCOM 20.0x) is the tightest match.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 16x NTM P/E is inside the range, ~55% below the 35x peer median and ~22% below the at-scale AVGO/TSM anchor (20.6x). NVDA itself trades at 19.3-19.7x NTM (Q3 FY27-Q2 FY28).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: A discount, not a premium. The high-median names (ARM, AMD, MRVL, ANET, equipment) are on early-ramp or depressed earnings, so their multiples are inflated; AVGO and TSM are the only peers at NVDA's scale and earnings stage. NVDA's earnings are near a cyclical peak with growth set to fall from ~+70% (FY28) to ~+15% (FY29), consensus hyperscaler capex growth slowing to ~+22% in 2027 (src 27), and 10Y yields at 5.24-5.28% with a Dec hike ~70-72% priced (src 26,14,15). The market already capitalises NVDA below AVGO/TSM (19.5x vs 20.6x) and has compressed it from ~25x in April; the top-dog base rate (src 19-20) argues the gap persists. Sell-side outperformance calls are not used.

thesis_break_reason: $165 is just above the 52-week low ($164.27) and ~10x the consistent-window Oct-2027 NTM EPS (~$16.7). Trading there would most likely mean FY28/FY29 earnings are being cut 25-30% (hyperscaler capex cut, memory-cost margin collapse, ASIC share loss), not 38%-vol noise or ordinary multiple compression, which in my base case stops near 16x.

key_uncertainties: Whether 2027 hyperscaler capex (~$1.3T across six, mostly FCF-negative) turns into a 2028 digestion
How far the multiple compresses: NTM P/E fell from ~40x (2025) to ~25x (Apr-2026) to ~19.5x now, estimate-driven; a flat year needs ~14.2x on my horizon EPS
Memory/HBM cost inflation versus NVDA's pricing power (Q4 GM 71-72%)
ASIC share gains (Google TPU, Broadcom/Marvell custom silicon)
Survivorship bias: NVDA's own 12m return history (median +40%) overstates what a $5.7T company can do
Cash conversion: Q2 FY27 FCF was only 36-39% of net income (DSO 60, $279B supply commitments); if it stays low, FCF-based value is well below P/E-based value
reasoning: Base rates first. NVDA's own 12-month forward returns since 2002: median +40%, P(down) 22%, P(<-40%) 7%; in setups like today (prior year +10-45%, at a 52-week high, n=25) median +29%. That record is survivorship-biased for a $5.7T leader; the top-dog base rate (Arnott/Wu: largest companies trail their sector by ~4%/yr) and a ~7% market return pull the centre to roughly +5-12%. Round-2 corrections from the supervisor, all accepted: (1) my horizon NTM EPS used a window shifted one quarter forward; on the same Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29 window as today's 19.3-19.7x it is ~$16.7 after a 5% haircut (also FY29 growth trimmed to +15% given consensus 2027 capex growth of only ~+22%, src 27); (2) my fair value used 18x while my base scenario used 15x; I now use one multiple, 16x, in both; (3) FCF conversion of 85% is not supported (Q2 FY27 FCF 36-39% of NI, H1 ~70%), now 75%, with ~$1/share true net cash; (4) the 10Y at 5.24-5.28% is verified at Treasury (src 26) but it is the highest since 2007, not 2002; (5) the Fed-odds source was misattributed; the Dec-9 meeting-specific Kalshi contract shows ~70% for a 25bp hike (search-result snapshot; direct fetch 429) and DeFi Rate 72%, so the macro headwind stands; (6) I dropped the 'historical 17-20x floor' argument. On compression: it has been estimate-driven (FY28 EPS +24% in 90 days while the price rose), so it is real but has not hurt holders; I assume 3.5 more turns (to 16x), while a flat year needs ~14.2x on my EPS, a de-rating that likely needs an EPS break. Fair value $255 (P/E $267, FCF $230, mid-cycle $260) is below my round-1 $296. Scenarios: bear $150 (25%), base $267 (50%), bull $342 (25%, lowered from $370 to an 18x multiple). The ladder is a three-lognormal mixture (sigmas 0.25/0.20/0.18) plus a 5% wide tail component: mean ~$263, median ~$262, P(up) ~61%, P(<$166) ~17%. The ladder sits slightly above the blended fair value because the FCF leg is a deliberately rate-harsh cross-check. Research limits: Kalshi returned 429 and Polymarket's December page was the 2025 market, so Fed odds rest on the Kalshi search snapshot and the DeFi Rate aggregator; the Moody's capex note returned 403. Peer forward EV/EBITDA is estimated from trailing figures and peer growth is 3-year CAGR.
